headline: Easy-run cardiac drift is dropping meaningfully — aerobic efficiency is visibly improving over the recent block.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The most notable signal in today's data isn't volume — it's the shift in how hard your heart is working at easy paces. Average HR on comparable easy efforts has dropped noticeably over the last four weeks relative to the prior block, which at steady pace suggests genuine aerobic adaptation rather than reduced effort. This is the kind of quiet, unglamorous progress that compounds well over time.

Volume is effectively flat — two almost identical four-week blocks back-to-back — which in the context of a 20-week unbroken streak reads as intentional consolidation rather than stagnation. You're absorbing a sustained load, not drifting. The 44 km long run from late June remains a meaningful anchor in the background: that kind of durability effort takes weeks to fully integrate, and the steady easy running since then is appropriate.

Strength frequency has ticked down slightly versus the prior block, which is worth noticing but not concerning at this level — five sessions in four weeks still represents consistent exposure. The bigger picture is that you're maintaining a full hybrid training load across running, strength, commuting, and background activity simultaneously, and the aerobic markers are moving in the right direction.
watch_items: Watch whether the easy-run HR trend continues to decline as the 44 km effort fully integrates — a further drop would confirm real aerobic adaptation rather than session-to-session variance.
Monitor whether strength frequency stabilises or drops further across the next block — five sessions is fine, but a continued downward drift would be worth addressing.
The lactate threshold test from July 2nd is the first data point in a new baseline series — pay attention to whether subsequent tests show progression, stability, or noise as the history accumulates.

Running streak is now tied at your personal best — whether you extend or reset, notice how you feel about continuity versus flexibility, since that tension can inform how you structure recovery going forward.

evidence_items.text: ▼ Easy-run HR averaging 147 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 6 vs 6 runs)
▲ 4-week volume 127 km vs 125 km prior block (+2%)
